additional_info.subject: ID0423590-DC/Si-D/MC-[ Y2/R9 313202799090] >> secc pilot is E << On Connector 2 CRM:02684000227
additional_info.body:
Hi Yan, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
I will explain a bit more in detail why this error occurred, be aware of the time difference:
This is when the customer plugged in the EV and goes from Available to Preparing:
Usually, what we see afterwards is the Authentication process but before the authentication, there is a process called SLAC which is the first communication process between EV and Charger.
In this process, it's only used the connectors from the plug.
After 5 secs, the customer plugged out resulting in a failed session
Since the process shouldn't be from B2 to A, the charger sent out a message of Error because afterwards, and the controller was unusable until a reboot:
From our side, this is clearly a interaction issue:
When we go from A → B2, the authentication is usually requested within 10-20sec see example below from your charger:
13sec
Here I can only say that the customer didn't wait long enough and the controller entered faulty state as it went through a process that is not supposed to.
If I answered to all your needs, let me know if I can close the ticket.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0423590-DC/Si-D/MC-[ Y2/R9 313202799090] >> secc pilot is E << On Connector 2 CRM:02684000227
additional_info.body:
Hello Yan,
Thank you for sharing your concerns. I will try to answer the best I can.
I see in OCPP Secc initializing as soon as gone in preparing, then faulted, and finally finishing 3 mins after
I do have a doubt on the user bad use, maybe a Cable issue, can it be? regularly this charger sends Secc's faulty messages
I don't believe it's a cable issue, I can see from our backend that there were ~100 sessions done in this charger with only the DC2 which is the one we are analyzing.
I also cannot confirm if it's a hardware issue since the communication was not established, the EV was plugged out too soon. If the EV plugged in and after 30sec it didn't work, I could confirm the possibility of a hardware issue, even though very unlikely since we have so many good sessions.
The Finishing came 3mins afterwards because the SECC didn't acknowledge as a session since the communication was not successfully established.
Let's consider the user did wrong (It may happen, we are only humans)
How can we track those faults?
Unfortunately, the error codes you see, are the only tracking you can do. Just like us, I don't just follow the error flag, I search throughout the whole session to understand start-to-finish and provide the best detailed answer as I can. You can also try to do that from your side, You see the Preparing and then Faulted, which means that an error occurred before the start charging.
It doesn't make sense to me, as on customer side, that a simple ineraction issue must occur in a charger reboot!!!!
I understand you are unhappy with this situation, this is not your usual fault, but I cannot confirm where the root cause lies since the logs are incomplete due to the crash of the session midway, which caused a possible firmware corruption and needed a restart.
for instance
1 car is charging
I try to plus and I miss, the second becomes faulty / Unavailable
Have I to wait the first car to finish charging, then reboot (mostly 10mins), then try again to charge?
To explain you a little bit more how the SECC works is the following:
It changes PilotState to the next one and when it either succeeds in ending a session or failing, it should always end in Error state. This is how the SECC is designed to work, to acknowledge that the session is over, only when there is an actual fail of the session, you get that SECC is in Pilot E, when the session ends successfully, you don't get it even though it's there.
So in this failed session that we currently discussing, we should've waited for the PilotState to change from B2 to E and not to A, so that the SECC could acknowledge a failed session.
You should always follow what the screen shows and from the logs, the screen should've been showing, communication establishing please wait 30sec. And if the session were a failure, it would ask please unplug and try again.
In this case, you wouldn't need to do a reboot.
Let me know if my answers were clear and please let me know your follow up questions :)
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
